verdict.tagline: Timeless sci-fi shooter brilliance, balanced by occasionally janky movement.
for_you_if: you want classic, demanding combat encounters
not_for_you_if: you need modern, precise movement controls
you are easily frustrated by complex level design

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players struggle with slippery movement and frustrating platforming.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the movement physics and sprint mechanics feel slippery or difficult to control, making platforming frustrating.

citations.review_text:
The pacing is glacial, the combat (especially melee) is clunky, and the atmosphere they're trying to create is let down by the technical limitations of the day. For example, the long intro sequence that was clearly meant to be captivating back in 1998 features dozens and dozens of scientists, but they cycle through ~4 unique character models so it feels like you're running into the same guys in every room. Worse still, the (I thought?) lauded movement system feels terrible. You sprint at double the typical speed but have directional control like you're moving through water, so platforming is a frustrating chore. I also get mild nausea from the FOV, but this game is way too old for an FOV slider. Perhaps there's a .cfg or .ini that would allow me to improve this, but it just doesn't seem to be worth it.

I never played this back in the day, so I have no nostalgia to influence me. This did not age well, and I will be refunding.

The movement physics are so bad they gave me a headache and the level design is rather unintuitive which is quite annoying. I cant say much about the story since I didnt get very far but it looked interesting so I am dissapointed that the movement makes it impossible to play for me. :(

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players praise the seamless environmental storytelling while citing stiff movement and difficult combat.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the movement controls as janky, slippery, or stiff.

citations.review_text: Besides the jank ass movement, good game

Half-Life is certainly a game that was revolutionary for its time but that does not mean it is without flaws. The story, weapon diversity, enemy ai, and visual design of the game all hold up very well despite Half-Life's age and I enjoyed them a lot but that enjoyment was lowered at times by the gameplay. During many of the sections requiring finer movement controlling Gordan felt like I was playing with a tungston brick on ice and during combat sections many of the guns experience a truly agonizing amount of bullet spread that makes even hitting relatively close targets a pain. Looking back on the time I spent on Half-Life I found that for around half of it I wasn't having any fun. To be clear I think its still a good game and I would still highly recommend it to those who won't be bothered by its jank the way I was. But for those who suspect it may detract from their experience with the game in the way it did for me I would recommend you play Black Mesa instead and then maybe come back to Half-Life later if your interested in the original game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features high difficulty, unforgiving combat encounters, and strict enemy aim.

citations.review_text: Half-Life is the best game ever made. It is extremely creative and well-written with fantastic combat and mechanics, I love all of it. I also love the immense difficulty of the game, especially on Hard mode. I'm barely a quarter through this game (first run on hard) and I have been put through hell, replaying segments with, for example, the soldiers, at least 30 times just to optimally beat it, and I loved every second of it. Some games make you feel powerful and unstoppable, but gordon freeman is literally just a guy. And you feel weak and helpless and terrified at points. That's one of the best things I love about it.

Game holds up surprisingly well nearly 3 decades later. interesting story, fast gunplay, good levels. 

Only complaint is the game VERY unforgiving. You will have certain saves where you have 1 hp, no ammo, and you need to make a run across a hallway. The catch is the npcs in this game actually have aimbot so you die the moment you show your face.

Good game.

I know I am I the absolute minority here. I never played this game until recently. I don't mind the dated visuals. The dated level design I am less keen on. I hated all the random surprises from hidden enemies. I hated all the random pitfalls and traps. I hated the ladders. I hated the omniscient enemy A.I. that will instantly snipe you if you so much as look at them from far away, even if they are looking the opposite direction. I didn't like the directionless nature of the objectives, though I can see the old-school appeal there for some. 

 If you're not save-scrumming this game I don't know how you're playing it for the first time. So many new-player traps. I can recognize Half-Life's place in gaming and FPS history but I just didn't find it fun to play now.

Finally worked up the courage to take it on again last week and WOW I was a moron back then. This game, while old, occasionally clunky, and certainly frustrating compared to modern games, is fantastic.

As if the gods knew I would love this game, Black Mesa went on sale on the same day I beat this game, so I expect another glowing review of that game to on the horizon.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the story unfolds naturally through the environment and gameplay without interruption from traditional cutscenes.

citations.review_text: To be fairly honest, Half-Life is an outstanding and truly *tremendous game*, quite frankly. I must say, the storytelling is amazing, and the gameplay really stands out. I especially love how there is no traditional dialogue or constant cutscenes. Instead, the story unfolds naturally around you, allowing you to experience everything firsthand. I enjoyed the fact that the game manages to keep you interested despite how old and outdated it might look. It just makes for an overall wholesome experience. I can definitely see why Half-Life is still so loved after all these years. Recommended.

Despite The Game’s Age, Half-Life Is still amazing, The Storytelling, Despite having no forced cutscenes, As in you can literally just kill the person you’re talking to for no reason, Is Good, And Some of the Enemies’ Ai Behaviours are still great, such as the Military Personnel. Easily some of Valve’s Best Work considering how Early it was released For Valve’s Existence

A timeless classic that still holds up incredibly well. Half-Life delivers an amazing atmosphere, immersive level design, and satisfying gameplay. The storytelling feels natural, letting you experience the world rather than constantly interrupting you with cutscenes.

Even after all these years, the game remains a fantastic experience. A true masterpiece that helped shape the FPS genre.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that certain later levels and chapters, such as On A Rail, Surface Tension, and Xen, feature confusing or frustrating level design.

citations.review_text: Either i accidentally picked the hard mode or this game is close to impossible, and so many bugs happened to me and some parts like on a rail had really unclear ways to actually progress. Also why can the stupid flying things shooting orange energy balls tank 2 crossbow shots while a vortigaunt dies in 2 pistol shots
Love the controller support, graphics, gameplay and such but man levels like surface tension are a nightmare. Amazing game though!

I really want to like half life regarding how much i love black mesa, but this game is so goddamn buggy and jank that its borderline unplayable. u literally die from doing nothing. elevators kill you, the cart in on a rail and apprehension kill you, you take fall damage from a 3 foot drop, etc, etc. the level design is also atrocious. on a rail, surface tension, and all xen chapters are perfect examples of this. the combat againts the aliens is painful ass well. its impossible to dodge vortigaunt attacks, which sucks cause they deal 20 health, head crabs have tiny hitboxes and are placed everywhere, and the alien grunts have like double the hp they should. i dont mind the old visuals, but they can get kinda annoying. at its best, the game still isnt as good as black mesa, and at its worst it can be unplayable. this game simply isnt fun to play, at least not today. go play black mesa instead. 5/10.

citations.review_text: Holy fucking hell, I grew up playing TF2, now play deadlock, but Valve continues to amaze me after all these years. This is a timeless master piece ,ad will janky and annoying, the setting, visuals, and story are nothing short of breathtaking (When considering the release date) 9/10, would highly recommend to any boomer shooter or story driven fans.

this aged, perfectly. the aestethic is so timeless. 
still worth playing it in this decade, this title from 1998, it's so surreal. It's aestethically so much a time capsule.

Can feel janky, but u get used to it and appreciate it. The level design is so iconic. Give this game 1 playthrough atleast. The sound design is, dare i say, flawless. it's so atmospheric. 
The Half-Life game series is a must play if you're into singleplayer stories.
 9.6/10.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game does not hold your hand.

citation.review_text:
I have owned this game for well over a decade now and the last time I played it must have been at least 5 years ago, originally I tried to rush through the game all those years ago which was a huge mistake because I just ended up dying constantly and getting lost and not understanding the mechanics of the game. This time I took my time and I have to say I really enjoyed every bit of it, the game does not hold your hand and is more difficult than modern FPS games but the game holds up well in my opinion, it always blows my mind how old games achieve such technical feats and its nice that the game has been updated to support modern hardware. The story is really interesting and I will definitely be playing more in the series now after this, I am super intrigued where this will go even if we don't have a conclusion but maybe one day we will? 

Either way I recommend people at least try this game, its one of the quintessential games of all time.

single_points.text: One reviewer likes that there isn't any way points or any indication where to go.

citation.review_text:

Besides that...
For a 1998 game, the graphics are decent (texture wise), but the models are what you'd exprct from a 1998 game. Imo the movement is frustrating sometimes, but only in those tricky slim parkour places. I do like that there isn't any way points or any indication where to go, even if I have to watch a tutorial sometimes, but that's what makes it fun. Overall, I recommend you play it first before playing half life 2, just so you know who freeman is and what happened at Black Mesa.
